note: STERILAMP trademark ('vacuum or gas-filled tubes employed for the generation of radiations') directly covers the technology in this stroboscopic lamp patent (H01J vacuum tube class); granted 1939-08-08, trademark filed 1939-08-25 — 17-day gap. Represents Westinghouse's UV/germicidal lamp product line commercialized under the STERILAMP brand.

MINALITE trademark ('incandescent electric lamps') corresponds to this hot cathode electron discharge tube patent (H01J vacuum tube class); granted 1931-10-27, trademark filed 1931-11-11 — 15-day gap. Represents Westinghouse's miniature lamp product line marketed under the MINALITE brand.

VICTOR trademark filed by RCA for 'radio apparatus, parts, and appurtenances—radio receiving sets, loudspeakers' just 28 days after this vacuum tube control patent was granted (H01J). Vacuum tubes were the core component of RCA's VICTOR-branded radio receivers; the 1924 filing date places this at the peak of early commercial radio, when RCA held a near-monopoly on radio set manufacture under its patent pool arrangement with GE and Westinghouse.
